WEATHER STORY:
Widely scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are expected on Thursday, with most of the activity south of I-90. Activity diminishes by sunset or so as the frontal boundary pushes into northern IL. Thereafter, a dry stretch of weather is in store at the latest,the first half of next week, as the storm pattern/jet stream pushes well north into Canada. Showers and storms may return by Thursday or Friday of next week as the storm jet sinks southward, allowing a frontal boundary to sag into northern WI or the UP. Currently, the higher chances are northeast of the area. These conditions continue for the following weekend (mainly dry), with thunderstorm complexes (late night/early AM and evening) tracking just to our north and east. Highs linger in the low 80s on Thursday and Friday, with a noticeable drop in humidity. We will see a slow warming trend through the weekend before temperatures climb back above average next week. After Monday, highs rise into the 90s for a few days in a row before falling back into the mid to upper 80s by the end of the week. While temperatures will be hot, the humidity levels will be considerably lower than during our early heatwave. This will make it feel much less miserable outside. WEATHER GRAPHICS:
